reason: Transfer/leakage lens. (1) Even a perfect version cannot pass the transfer gate. The GT-oracle survivor ceiling is +0.0004 on 44b6 and +0.0020 on 6bba. The 44b6 figure is already below the per-embryo gate of +0.001, so the idea fails 'each embryo >= +0.001' at the oracle. 44b6 is also overlapping crops of one recording, so most of its videos tie and the win-rate criterion cannot be met. About 83% of the ceiling comes from one embryo (6bba, with dense 13-15% labels) and almost all of it is FP removal. That profile is the kind of embryo-specific gain that does not carry over to the private embryos. (2) The head-gated arm acts only where there is no value. The x138 head moves peaks by a mean of 0.74 um, max 1.61 um. For two peaks to end up within 2.0 um, their raw distance must be at most 2 + 2 x shift: about 3.5 um at the mean shift, and 5.2 um only if both peaks move the maximum distance straight toward each other. With the 3 um NMS floor, the merges fall almost entirely in the 3-4 um band. There the oracle is -0.0003 / +0.0001, while the evaluable value sits in the 4-5 um band, which the head cannot close. The head-free versions (trajectory, prob, component length) measured -0.002 to -0.013 even with an in-sample detector, so they would do worse on unseen embryos. (3) Leakage inflates the 'same-nucleus' test locally. Both the UNet features and the x138 head (trained on 20 train movies; retraining on all 199 is being considered) are in-sample at the annotated points. So both peaks near an annotated nucleus get pulled toward the memorised GT point. Refined convergence, and 'merged point within 4 um of GT', will fire preferentially at annotated nuclei locally, which is exactly where the metric is evaluated. Neither the proposed step 0 nor the SELECTION/CONFIRMATION split can detect this, because the head is in-sample on every fold. (4) What remains is mostly the node-count multiplier. Merges limited to the 3-4 um band touch well under 0.5% of nodes: about +0.0001 to +0.0004 through 0.1 x dN/N, with near-zero edge value. The LB has already shown node-count effects that looked positive offline and reversed (min-track-length +0.013 offline, -0.004 public). (5) Private risk from divisions. Only 23 of 151 GT divisions are detected forks, so 'exclude forks and the 2 frames after' leaves most real sister pairs (3-6 um apart right after mitosis) unprotected. A head that pulls each sister about 1 um inward can merge them. That costs the edge, and it costs division-J headroom on embryos at a more mitotic stage.
fix_if_any: No version of this idea is worth an LB slot before 29 Sep. If the head capture exists anyway, run step 0 as a cheap diagnostic only. (a) Measure convergence on unannotated and annotated peaks separately. If the convergence rate at GT-matched pairs is more than 1.5x the rate elsewhere, treat it as leakage and stop. (b) Use a head trained on a disjoint set of videos (GroupKFold by embryo, 6bba-trained head scored on 44b6). (c) Additionally protect every pair whose members both have predecessors more than 3 um apart at t-1 (the sister/twin signature), not just detected forks. (d) Report the node-ratio change separately from edge J, and require the edge-J delta (without the node factor) to be > 0 on BOTH embryos. Ship only as a free rider in a bundle that already passes on its own, never as its own probe.
realistic_public_gain: About 0 (-0.001..+0.0005). The head-gated merges fall in the 3-4 um band, where the oracle is -0.0003/+0.0001, plus a node-multiplier term of at most about +0.0004. That is far below the +-0.003 resolution of the public LB. The head-free version is negative (-0.002..-0.013 locally with an in-sample detector, likely worse on private).
